entities.name: Caroline
entities.description: A transgender woman originally from Sweden, who moved to her current country around 2019 and began transitioning around 2020. One of the two speakers, a close friend of Melanie. She paints, draws and makes stained glass, plays acoustic guitar, is learning the piano, reads widely, and is pursuing a career in counseling and mental health. Through 2023 she attended an LGBTQ support group, an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop, pride parades, a transgender conference and a transgender poetry reading, mentored an LGBTQ teenager, joined the activist group Connected LGBTQ Activists, volunteered at an LGBTQ+ youth centre, and pursued adoption as a single parent, passing the adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023. She keeps a guinea pig called Oscar.

entities.name: Melanie
entities.description: The other speaker, a married mother of several children and a close friend of Caroline. Married since around 2018; her family keeps a dog, Oliver, and cats Luna and Bailey. She has made art for about seven years, painting landscapes, still life and animals, took up pottery in July 2023, runs to de-stress, plays the violin and the clarinet, and takes her family camping, hiking and to the beach. She ran a charity race for mental health in May 2023, volunteered with her family at a homeless shelter in August 2023, was injured in September 2023 and had to break off pottery, and went on a road trip in October 2023 during which her son was in a car accident.

entities.name: Melanie's husband
entities.description: Melanie's husband, married to her since around 2018; she described marrying him and promising to be together forever as the best part of her wedding day. He appears in family photographs with the children and is one of the people who keep her motivated. The conversation never gives his name.

entities.name: Melanie's children

properties.aliases: the kids; my kids; my fam; my family

entities.description: A group entity for Melanie's children, referred to constantly and named individually never. There are at least three: a son who was in a car accident on the October 2023 road trip, a daughter whose birthday was celebrated at a concert on 13 August 2023, a youngest daughter whose first steps Melanie remembers, and 'the 2 younger kids' who love nature. They go camping, hiking and to the beach with their parents, painted and made pottery with Melanie, and visited a museum and a park in the summer of 2023.

entities.name: Caroline's friends, family and mentors

properties.aliases: my friends, family and mentors; my support system; my rocks; the gang

entities.description: A group entity for the people Caroline calls her rocks: friends she has known for four years, since she moved from Sweden around 2019, along with her family and her mentors. She credits them with carrying her through her transition and a tough breakup, and they appear across the whole conversation — at a meet-up in June 2023, a picnic in early July 2023, and a day out biking over the weekend of 9-10 September 2023. She said in September 2023 that some close friends kept supporting her through her transition while a few could not handle it.

entities.name: Amy Ellis Nutt
entities.description: The author of 'Becoming Nicole', the book Caroline named on 12 July 2023 as her favourite guide.

entities.name: Sara Bareilles
entities.description: The singer of 'Brave', the song Caroline said on 28 August 2023 has particular significance for her.

entities.name: Oscar
entities.description: Caroline's guinea pig, mentioned on 23 August 2023 as her pet and as great company; parsley and vegetables are his favourite food.

entities.name: Oliver
entities.description: Melanie's dog, one of the household's pets along with the cat Luna and, from August 2023, a second cat called Bailey. Melanie said he once hid his bone in her slipper.

entities.name: Luna
entities.description: Melanie's cat, one of two pets along with the dog Oliver when Melanie introduced them on 12 July 2023; a second cat, Bailey, had arrived by 23 August 2023.

entities.name: Bailey
entities.description: The second cat in Melanie's household, which she reported having got when she spoke to Caroline on 23 August 2023, making three pets with the dog Oliver and the cat Luna.

entities.name: Sweden
entities.description: Caroline's home country, which she left around 2019. Her grandmother, who gave her the necklace she treasures, lives there.

entities.name: the Grand Canyon
entities.description: The place Melanie's children enjoyed on the family road trip over the weekend of 14-15 October 2023.

entities.name: Caroline's LGBTQ support group
entities.description: The LGBTQ support group Caroline attended on 7 May 2023 and found powerful, where transgender members' stories inspired her. She credits it with making her feel accepted and giving her the courage to embrace herself, and with starting her interest in counseling as a career.

entities.name: Connected LGBTQ Activists
entities.description: The LGBTQ activist group Caroline joined on 18 July 2023. She described it as made up of all kinds of people investing in positive change, holding regular meetings and planning events and campaigns.

entities.name: the LGBTQ youth mentorship program
entities.description: The mentorship program for LGBTQ youth Caroline joined over the weekend of 15-16 July 2023. Through it she mentors a transgender teenager whose experience resembles her own, working with them on confidence and positive strategies; the two attended an LGBT pride event together in June 2023.

entities.name: the LGBTQ+ youth centre

properties.aliases: the youth center; an LGBTQ center

entities.description: The LGBTQ+ youth centre where Caroline volunteered shortly before 28 August 2023 and said she would carry on volunteering, and where she and the staff were putting together a talent show for the young people in September 2023. Joined here with the 'LGBTQ center' Caroline said on 17 July 2023 she had visited before painting the piece for her art show, on the strength of the same description and the same period; the conversation never names either.

entities.name: Caroline's adoption agency

properties.aliases: the adoption agency; one of the adoption agencies I'm looking into

entities.description: The adoption agency Caroline picked out in May 2023 because it helps LGBTQ+ people adopt, and whose inclusivity and support spoke to her. She applied in the week up to 23 August 2023 and passed its interviews on 20 October 2023. The conversation never names it.

entities.name: Melanie's pottery class
entities.description: The pottery class Melanie signed up for on 2 July 2023 and attended through the summer, making a black-and-white bowl with a flower design, a brightly coloured and patterned bowl, and a flower-decorated plate. She had to take a break from pottery after being injured in September 2023.

entities.name: Charlotte's Web
entities.description: The book Melanie named on 6 July 2023 as her favourite from childhood, because it showed how friendship and compassion can make a difference.

entities.name: Becoming Nicole
entities.description: The book by Amy Ellis Nutt that Caroline named on 12 July 2023 as her favourite guide: a true story about a trans girl and her family that made her feel connected, gave her hope for her own path, and taught her self-acceptance and how to find support. She recommended it to Melanie.

entities.name: Brave
entities.description: The Sara Bareilles song Caroline said on 28 August 2023 has a lot of significance for her, because it is about being courageous and fighting for what is right and makes her think about the path she has taken.

entities.name: Embracing Identity
entities.description: Caroline's painting of a woman, shown to Melanie on 14 August 2023. Caroline said it is about finding comfort and love in being yourself, that the woman stands for the journey of acceptance, and that she meant it to show warmth, love and self-acceptance.

entities.name: Caroline's grandmother's necklace
entities.description: A necklace with a cross and a heart that Caroline's grandmother in Sweden gave her when she was young. Caroline said on 27 June 2023 that it stands for love, faith and strength and reminds her of her roots and her family's support.

entities.name: Caroline's hand-painted bowl
entities.description: A hand-painted bowl a friend made for Caroline's 18th birthday around 2013. She named it on 27 June 2023 as a possession with sentimental value, whose pattern and colours remind her of art and self-expression.

entities.name: painting
entities.description: The art both women practise and the subject of much of the conversation. Melanie paints landscapes, still life, sunsets and animals, has made art for about seven years and paints with her children; Caroline has made art since she was about 17 and paints her trans experience, self-portraits, sunsets, flowers and abstracts, exhibiting at an LGBTQ art show.

entities.name: pottery
entities.description: Melanie's craft, taken up on 2 July 2023 and described by her as therapy, a sanctuary and a huge part of her life rather than just a hobby. She made bowls, a plate and took her children to a pottery workshop, and broke off after an injury in September 2023. Caroline had still not tried it as of 13 September 2023 but was willing to.

entities.name: running
entities.description: Melanie's way of de-stressing and clearing her mind, part of the daily me-time she carved out from May 2023. She ran a charity race for mental health on 20 May 2023, had been running longer distances by July 2023, and bought new running shoes around then.

entities.name: camping
entities.description: Melanie's family tradition and the highlight of their summer: marshmallows, campfire stories and nature. Trips mentioned include the mountains in June 2023, the beach, the forest, a weekend on 8-9 July 2023, one a few weeks before mid-September 2023, and one in 2022 when they watched the Perseid meteor shower.

entities.name: hiking
entities.description: Walking in the mountains and forests, which Melanie's family do together and which Caroline also does; it was on a hike in mid-August 2023 that Caroline had an upsetting encounter with a group of religious conservatives.

entities.name: reading
entities.description: A pastime of both women. Caroline says books guide and motivate her and is building a children's library for the children she hopes to adopt; Melanie reads as part of her daily me-time and read a book in 2022 that reminds her to pursue her dreams.

entities.name: playing the guitar
entities.description: Caroline's instrument. She started playing acoustic guitar about five years before 28 August 2023, around 2018, and says it helps her get her emotions out.

entities.name: LGBTQ advocacy
entities.description: Caroline's advocacy work for the LGBTQ and trans community: speaking at a school event in June 2023, attending pride parades, an LGBTQ conference on 10 July 2023 and a transgender poetry reading on 6 October 2023, joining Connected LGBTQ Activists, mentoring LGBTQ youth, volunteering at an LGBTQ+ youth centre, and using her art to speak up for the community.

entities.name: Caroline's gender transition
entities.description: Caroline began transitioning around 2020, three years before June 2023, and speaks about it throughout the conversation. She describes coming out, the struggles and growth since, the courage it took, art as a way of exploring her changing body and identity, and the friends, family and mentors who carried her through it; some close friends stayed and a few could not handle it.

entities.name: Caroline's adoption
entities.description: Caroline's undertaking to adopt as a single parent, a long-held dream of giving a loving home to children in need. It ran from researching LGBTQ-friendly agencies by 25 May 2023, through a council meeting on adoption on 14 July 2023, applying to agencies in the week up to 23 August 2023 and contacting her mentor for advice on 13 October 2023, to passing the agency interviews on 20 October 2023.

entities.name: Caroline's LGBTQ art show
entities.description: An art show of Caroline's paintings featuring LGBTQ artists, which she is putting together and which she hoped would spread understanding and acceptance. She said on 17 July 2023 it would be the following month, and on 25 August 2023 that it would be the following month again, in September 2023.

entities.name: Caroline's move into counseling and mental health
entities.description: Caroline's pursuit of a career in counseling or mental health work, raised in nearly every session from 8 May 2023 onward. She wants to work with trans people, helping them accept themselves and supporting their mental health, because her own struggles and the support she received showed her what a support system is worth. She attended an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on 23 June 2023 and continued to say she was still working out the details.

claims.text: Caroline got in touch with Melanie on 20 July 2023 to say hello and catch up.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline joined a new LGBTQ activist group on 18 July 2023 and was meeting people as passionate as she is about rights and community support; she said it let her give her voice and make a real difference and was fulfilling.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 20 July 2023 that her activist group is called 'Connected LGBTQ Activists', that it is made up of all kinds of people investing in positive changes, and that it holds regular meetings and plans events and campaigns.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline's city held a pride parade over the weekend of 15-16 July 2023, with people marching through the streets waving flags and holding signs; Caroline missed it but said on 20 July 2023 that it was a powerful reminder that they are not alone in the fight for equality and inclusivity.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie took her children to the beach shortly before 20 July 2023 and said they had a blast.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 July 2023 that seeing her children's happy faces at the beach was the best part, and that the family only goes once or twice a year, which makes those trips special.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 July 2023 that the family's camping trip is the highlight of their summer and something they always look forward to, with marshmallows, campfire stories and each other's company.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 July 2023 that her best camping memory is the family's trip in 2022, when they watched the Perseid meteor shower under a clear sky, made wishes and felt at one with the universe.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 July 2023 that she will never forget the day her youngest daughter took her first steps, which showed her how fleeting life is and how lucky she is to share such moments.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 July 2023 that moments like these make her appreciate life and that she feels lucky to have her family, who bring her joy and love.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie celebrated her daughter's birthday at a concert on the evening of 13 August 2023, surrounded by music and joy in the warm summer breeze, and said seeing her children's smiles made her thankful for their moments together.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 14 August 2023 that the concert she took her daughter to was by Matt Patterson, and that she thought his voice and songs were amazing.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 14 August 2023 that an advocacy event she had been to was a cool experience with a lot of love and support.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline went to a pride parade on 11 August 2023 and found it full of energy and love, with people of all kinds celebrating acceptance; it made her proud and pushed her to keep standing up for LGBTQ equality.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 14 August 2023 that representing inclusivity and diversity in her art matters to her and that she uses her art to speak up for the LGBTQ+ community and push for acceptance.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 14 August 2023 that her art is about expressing her trans experience, showing her story and helping people understand the trans community.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline showed Melanie her painting 'Embracing Identity' on 14 August 2023 and said it is about finding comfort and love in being yourself, that the woman in it stands for the journey of acceptance, and that she aimed to show warmth, love and self-acceptance.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 14 August 2023 that art has let her explore her transition and her changing body, that it is a good way to work through what she is going through, and that it teaches her to accept the beauty of imperfections.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline had an upsetting encounter with a group of religious conservatives while out on a hike shortly before 17 August 2023; what they said made her think how much work remains to be done for LGBTQ rights, though she said the people who accept and support her meant she would be all right.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie finished another pottery project shortly before 17 August 2023 and showed Caroline a photograph of the colourful bowl that day, saying she was proud of it and that it had been a great experience.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 17 August 2023 that she chose bold colours and patterns for the bowl because she is obsessed with them and wanted to catch the eye and make people smile, and that painting lets her express her feelings, with each stroke carrying a part of her.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 17 August 2023 that she has always felt a strong connection to art, that it has been a huge learning experience, and that it is both a sanctuary and a source of comfort.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie agreed on 17 August 2023 that holding on to the things that bring happiness is what keeps them going when life is hard, and each said the other makes life's struggles more bearable.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie went to a Pride festival together with a group of friends in 2022, which both remembered on 17 August 2023 as a blast.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie agreed on 17 August 2023 to plan something special together for the summer of 2023 — either a family outing or a trip for the two of them to catch up and explore nature — and Melanie said she would start thinking about what they could do.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline applied to adoption agencies in the week up to 23 August 2023, calling it her first step towards becoming a mother, and said she had had a lot of help from an adoption advice and assistance group she attended.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that having applied to adopt felt exciting but nerve-wracking, because parenting is such a big responsibility.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that she has a guinea pig called Oscar who has been great company, and showed Melanie a photograph of him eating parsley, saying vegetables are his favourite.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie said on 23 August 2023 that her pets were doing well and that the household had got another cat, named Bailey, alongside the dog Oliver and the cat Luna.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 23 August 2023 that the funniest thing her dog Oliver had done was hide his bone in her slipper, and mentioned that she had once fed a horse a carrot.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that she used to go horseback riding through the fields with her father when she was a child, that it felt special, and that she has always loved horses.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie painted a horse on a wooden wall shortly before 23 August 2023 and showed it to Caroline, saying she loves painting animals because it is peaceful and special and horses have such grace.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline painted a self-portrait in the week before 23 August 2023 and showed it to Melanie, saying she loves creating art and that painting is great for expressing herself.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that painting her self-portrait left her feeling liberated and empowered, and that painting helps her explore her identity, be true to herself and is therapeutic.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that art gives her a sense of freedom, as do having supportive people around her, promoting LGBTQ rights and being true to herself, and that she wants to live authentically and help others do the same.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 23 August 2023 that she was excited for the future as her adoption went ahead, and Melanie wished her the best on the adoption journey.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline went hiking in the week before 25 August 2023 and got into a bad situation with some people that really bugged her, after which she tried to apologise to them.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie made a plate decorated with flowers in her pottery class on 24 August 2023 and showed it to Caroline the next day, saying pottery is relaxing and creative.

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that she had not tried pottery and had been busy painting instead.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline painted a sunset after visiting the beach in the week before 25 August 2023, wanting to capture the calm of the sun dipping below the horizon, and showed the finished painting to Melanie, who said it conveyed serenity.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie spent 24 August 2023 volunteering at a homeless shelter with her family; she found it hard to see how neglected some people were but felt they could make a difference.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that finding a community where she is accepted, loved and supported has meant a great deal and made a huge difference, because the people in it understand what she is going through.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that a rainbow flag mural painted with an eagle is special to her: the mural reflects the courage and strength of the trans community and the eagle symbolises freedom and pride, and her own resilience.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline made a stained glass window for a local church showing time changing our lives, and told Melanie on 25 August 2023 that she made it to reflect her own journey as a transgender woman and the idea that we should accept growth and change, and to remind people that the key to their potential is within them.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that her stained glass window is a symbol of togetherness and celebrating differences, and that she would love to make something like it again.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline came across a rainbow-painted sidewalk laid for Pride Month while walking in her neighbourhood and photographed it; she told Melanie on 25 August 2023 that it was vibrant and welcoming and reminded her that love and acceptance are everywhere, even where you least expect them.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that she had recently seen someone drawing a flower on the ground and that it made her happy, since creativity can lighten someone's day.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that art gives her joy, lets her show her feelings and freeze beautiful moments, and that drawing flowers is one of her favourite things to do.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie said on 25 August 2023 that painting landscapes and still life is her favourite kind of art, showed Caroline a recent sunflower painting, and said she was feeling inspired by autumn and planning a few more paintings.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 25 August 2023 that she was putting together an LGBTQ art show for the following month, September 2023, at which she would show her paintings alongside other LGBTQ artists, and that she wanted it to spread understanding and acceptance.

claims.text: Melanie took her children to a park on 27 August 2023, where they had fun exploring and playing outdoors.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline volunteered at an LGBTQ+ youth centre shortly before 28 August 2023 and found talking with young people like herself gratifying; it reminded her how essential it is to be kind and show support.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 28 August 2023 that she was struck by how strong the young people at the youth centre were despite their challenges, that she felt fulfilled guiding and supporting them, and that sharing her own story so they would know they are not alone was a powerful and emotional experience which reminded her of her own past loneliness.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 28 August 2023 that she would carry on volunteering at the LGBTQ+ youth centre, which is an important part of her life and where she has made strong connections, because she believes in community and supporting each other.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 28 August 2023 that the LGBTQ+ youth centre was putting together a talent show for the young people in September 2023, and that she was looking forward to seeing them enjoy it and feel proud of their talents.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie went to an outdoor concert in a park shortly before 28 August 2023 and said it was great fun and reminded her how music brings people together.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 28 August 2023 that playing and singing let her express herself and connect with others, and that she finds music cathartic and uplifting.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 28 August 2023 that the guitar is mostly her instrument and helps her get her emotions out, and that she started playing acoustic guitar about five years earlier, around 2018.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 28 August 2023 that 'Brave' by Sara Bareilles has a lot of significance for her because it is about being courageous and fighting for what is right, and that hearing it makes her think about the paths she has taken and the progress she has made.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie said on 28 August 2023 that she plays the clarinet, which she started when she was young, and that it is a way to express herself and relax.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 28 August 2023 that she likes both classical music such as Bach and Mozart and modern music such as Ed Sheeran's 'Perfect'.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline spent a day out with her friends over the weekend of 9-10 September 2023, going biking and seeing the sights, and found it refreshing; she shared a photograph of a beach at sunset with Melanie on 13 September 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie went camping with her children a few weeks before 13 September 2023, exploring the forest and hiking, and said nature can be refreshing for the soul.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 13 September 2023 that watching her children get excited about learning something new in nature makes being a parent worth it, and that roasting marshmallows and sharing stories round the campfire make the best memories.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 September 2023 that she is inspired by seeing her work make a difference for the LGBTQ+ community, that knowing she is helping create a more loving world is amazing, and that she is thankful for the support of her friends, family and mentors, which inspires her to keep making art.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 September 2023 that she has been creating art since she was about 17, and that she finds it empowering and cathartic because art can show things that are hard to put into words.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie said on 13 September 2023 that she had been into art for seven years, since around 2016, and that painting and pottery are her real muses because they are calming and satisfying.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 September 2023 that painting and drawing have helped her express her feelings and explore her gender identity, and that creating art was really important to her during her transition because it helped her understand and accept herself.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 September 2023 that she had still not done pottery but was game for trying new art forms and might try it sometime.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline made a red and blue painting about her path as a trans woman and showed it to Melanie on 13 September 2023: the red and blue stand for the binary gender system and the mixing of the colours for smashing that rigid thinking, and it reminds her to love her authentic self after a long journey to being proud of who she is.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 September 2023 that her transition changed her relationships: some close friends kept supporting her while a few could not handle it, and though it was not easy she is much happier among people who accept and love her and her relationships now feel more genuine.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie had a good time at a café over the weekend of 9-10 September 2023 and told Caroline about a sign on its door on 13 September 2023; when Caroline was alarmed by it, Melanie said it was only a precaution and that she had enjoyed herself.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline contacted her mentor for adoption advice on 13 October 2023, saying she was ready to be a mother and to share her love and a family, and that it had long been her dream to adopt and provide a safe, loving home for children who need it.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie said on 13 October 2023 that a friend of hers had adopted a child in 2022 after a long process and was now very happy with the child, and that it made her feel she might do it too; Caroline offered to help if she did.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline advised Melanie on 13 October 2023 to research and find an adoption agency or lawyer, to gather references, financial information and medical checks, and to prepare emotionally because the wait can be hard.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie was hurt in September 2023 and had to take a break from pottery, which she uses for self-expression and peace; she told Caroline on 13 October 2023 that it had been tough but she was doing all right.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 13 October 2023 that she had been keeping busy while off pottery by painting and by reading a book Caroline had recommended to her earlier in 2023.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie painted a sunset with a pink sky in the week before 13 October 2023 because the colours made her feel calm, and showed it to Caroline.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 October 2023 that she had been trying abstract work recently, finding it freeing to put her feelings on the canvas without much of a plan.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie showed Caroline an abstract painting of hers on 13 October 2023 and said she wanted peaceful blue streaks to convey tranquillity, because blue calms her, while keeping vibrant colours.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline went to a transgender poetry reading on 6 October 2023 at which transgender people shared their stories through poetry; she found it powerful and empowering and valued it as a safe place for self-expression.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 13 October 2023 that the room at the transgender poetry reading was electric with energy and support and that the posters of pride and strength there inspired her to make some art.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline drew a woman in a dress after the transgender poetry reading and told Melanie on 13 October 2023 that it stands for freedom and being real and reminds her to stay true to herself and embrace her womanhood.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie agreed on 13 October 2023 that being yourself is an ongoing adventure of learning and growing and that they were glad to be on it together.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie and her family went on a road trip over the weekend of 14-15 October 2023 during which her son was in an accident; he was all right, but the whole family was frightened by it.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that the road trip got off to a bad start, that she was really scared when they had the accident, and that her son being all right was a reminder that life is precious and to cherish her family.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that the accident had made her think about how much she needs her family and how thankful she is for them, and that her children had enjoyed the Grand Canyon on the road trip.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that her other children were scared by the accident but were reassured that their brother would be all right, and that they are tough.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that her children's resilience is greater than her own and that they give her the strength to keep going, being her biggest motivation and support.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie agreed on 20 October 2023 that Melanie's family are her rock and that having people to lean on helps in tougher times.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie and her children walked a trail on 19 October 2023 as a way to relax after the road trip, and the children loved it.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that nature helps her reset and recharge and that she loves camping trips with her family because nature brings peace and serenity.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Melanie said on 20 October 2023 that what she loves most about camping is the chance to be present together, bonding over stories, campfires and nature, and waking to birdsong and fresh air.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline passed the adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023, a big move towards her goal of having a family, and told Melanie on 22 October 2023 that she was excited and thankful.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie bought wooden figurines on 21 October 2023 that remind her of family love.
claims.speaker: Melanie

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that the figurines brought home how much love there is in families, both blood families and chosen ones, and that she hopes to build her own family and give a home to children who have not had one, adoption being for her a way of giving back and showing love and acceptance.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that her dream is to create a safe and loving home for the children she adopts, because love and acceptance should be everyone's right.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that finding self-acceptance had been a long process and that she was now ready to offer love and support to those who need it, which she finds empowering.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that transitioning and finding acceptance were both hard, that the help of her friends, family and the people she looked up to was invaluable in getting her through and finding out who she really was, and that she wants to pass that support on to anyone who needs it.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline said on 22 October 2023 that she is grateful to be able to share her journey and help others with theirs, and that the encouragement of those close to her made her who she is.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline and Melanie agreed on 22 October 2023 that being yourself and living honestly is freeing and lets a person accept who they are and be content.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline's adoption went from researching LGBTQ-friendly agencies by 25 May 2023, through a council meeting on adoption on 14 July 2023 and applying to agencies in the week up to 23 August 2023, to passing the adoption agency interviews on 20 October 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Caroline's involvement in the LGBTQ community deepened across 2023: from attending a support group on 7 May 2023, she went on to mentor a transgender teenager from mid-July 2023, join the activist group Connected LGBTQ Activists on 18 July 2023, and volunteer at an LGBTQ+ youth centre by late August 2023.
claims.speaker: Caroline

claims.text: Melanie added pottery to her painting in the summer of 2023: she signed up for a class on 2 July 2023, took her children to a pottery workshop on 14 July 2023, made bowls and a flower-decorated plate through July and August 2023, and then had to break off after being hurt in September 2023.
claims.speaker: Melanie
